clue.text: Object to work by model

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
to model is to pose, as for an artist

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to work for a particular model.
explanation.definitionFit: To object to something is to resist or set yourself against it.

clue.text: After working, student starts Year One

indicators.note: the student comes after the word for working

parts.note: a machine that is on is working
L is a learner driver

indicators.note: the starting letter of the word Year

parts.note: the first letter of the word Year

explanation.surface: Once their job is sorted, a student begins first year.
explanation.definitionFit: 'My one hope' and 'my only hope' mean the same: single and sole.

clue.text: Audio image of jug?

indicators.note: heard rather than seen, so the word for image is taken by its sound

parts.note: a picture is an image

explanation.surface: A recording that conjures up a picture of a jug.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitcher is a large jug with a lip and handle for pouring.

clue.text: Nottingham Forest, showing heart initially, sadly drew 0-0

indicators.note: takes the initial letter of each of the two words before it

parts.note: the first letters of the two words showing and heart

indicators.note: the letters are arranged in a sorry new order

parts.note: taken as written
two noughts read as two letter Os

explanation.surface: Nottingham Forest football club showed spirit early but disappointingly drew nil-nil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nottingham Forest' looks like the football club; it is the actual forest, home of Robin Hood.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherwood is the royal forest in Nottinghamshire famed from the Robin Hood legends.

clue.text: Sum up sailor's art going back to the beginnings of Christian times

parts.note: AB, able seaman, with the possessive S

indicators.note: the word art is read in the backward direction

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of each of the two words that follow

parts.note: the first letters of the two words Christian and times

explanation.surface: A summary of a sailor's art that dates back to early Christian times.
explanation.walkthrough: AB is an able-bodied seaman; the 's of sailor's stays as an S.
explanation.definitionFit: An abstract is a summary, so to abstract is to condense a document into its main points.

clue.text: Buys a larger boiled sweet?

indicators.note: boiling breaks the letters down and reshapes them

parts.note: these three words supply the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A shopper picks up a bigger boiled sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boiled' does double duty in the surface: barley sugar is itself a boiled sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Barley sugar is a hard amber confection made from boiled sugar.

clue.text: Artist takes top off paint, stirring it in

indicators.note: stirring mixes the letters together into a new order
in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter, which is removed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A painter opens a tin of paint and stirs it.
explanation.definitionFit: Titian was the great sixteenth-century Venetian painter.

clue.text: Circus performer uses wild boar in routine

indicators.note: the rearranged animal goes inside the routine

parts.note: an act is a performer's routine

indicators.note: a wild boar runs out of control, so its letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A circus performer works a wild pig into the show.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrobat is a gymnast who performs feats of balance and agility, typically in a circus.

clue.text: Inserting chart after carriage return makes it easy to manipulate

indicators.note: the chart is placed after the carriage piece
the word for carriage comes back the other way

parts.note: a cart is a carriage
a table is a chart of data

explanation.surface: Instructions for typing a chart after pressing the carriage return key in a document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carriage return' looks like the typewriter key; the two words are split.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tractable is docile and easily controlled or managed.

clue.text: Correspondence with landlord?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a written message sent by post
second meaning: one who lets property, hence the question mark

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a whimsical coinage: someone who lets a room is a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a written message, and playfully also a person who rents out property.

clue.text: Intelligence agency incorporates formal practice with right standards

indicators.note: the agency takes the other pieces into its own body, so they go inside it

parts.note: the CIA is the US intelligence agency
a rite is a formal ceremonial practice

explanation.surface: A spy agency adopting proper procedure and the right benchmarks.
explanation.definitionFit: Criteria are the standards or tests by which something is judged.

clue.text: Breathe with bit of distress, having been chased by Alice

indicators.note: letters in distress are knocked out of shape and rearranged

parts.note: these three words supply the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone gasping a little in distress after being pursued by a woman named Alice.
explanation.walkthrough: In Alice's Adventures in Wonderland Alice follows this character down the rabbit hole.
explanation.definitionFit: The waistcoated creature with a pocket watch is the one Alice pursues in Lewis Carroll's story.

clue.text: Bigotry based in ancient lore

indicators.note: the letters are built on anew, rearranged into a new word

parts.note: these two words supply the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Prejudice that has its roots in old traditions.
explanation.definitionFit: Intolerance is unwillingness to accept views or people different from your own, the essence of bigotry.

clue.text: She waits above to assist hero in trouble

indicators.note: letters in trouble are thrown into disorder and rearranged

parts.note: these two words supply the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman stands by ready to help a hero who is in a fix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waits' means serves as a waiter does, and 'above' means in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight attendant serves passengers on an aircraft, waiting on them high above the ground.

clue.text: Commercial expedition gains acceptance

parts.note: a commercial is an advertisement, an ad
a mission is an expedition with a purpose

explanation.surface: A business trip gets approved.
explanation.definitionFit: Admission is being allowed in, accepted into a place or group.

clue.text: Pierce is in reverse

indicators.note: in reverse means the word for being in at cricket is read backwards

parts.note: in cricket the side that is in bats

explanation.surface: A man named Pierce is retreating.
explanation.walkthrough: Pierce looks like a name; it is a verb meaning to stab.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce something is to puncture it with a pointed weapon or tool.

clue.text: Witch's assistant is well known

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a spirit, often an animal, serving a witch
second meaning: commonly known or recognised

explanation.walkthrough: A witch's cat is the classic example of the first sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a witch's attendant spirit and also describes something recognisable.

clue.text: Dumb show is part of the medium I'm exploiting

indicators.note: the answer is a part of the run of letters in the words that follow

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of medium, all of I'm and the start of exploiting

explanation.surface: A silent performance is how this medium is being put to use.
explanation.definitionFit: A dumb show is wordless acting, which is what a mime performance is.

clue.text: I go with badly spoken girl on ramble

parts.note: ME is the object form of I
and joins one thing with another

indicators.note: said carelessly, the way a Londoner drops the aitch from the word for a girl

parts.note: her refers to a girl

explanation.surface: Someone sets off on a walk with a girl who speaks poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the aitch, the phrase 'me and 'er' runs together into one word.
explanation.definitionFit: To meander is to wander aimlessly, taking a winding course, much as a ramble does.

clue.text: Delay before I get top grade in award for making crib

indicators.note: the delay, I and grade are placed inside the award

parts.note: a prize is an award

indicators.note: the delay comes ahead of I

parts.note: to lag is to fall behind
taken as written
A is the highest exam grade

explanation.surface: A student holds off, wins top marks and earns a prize for copying.
explanation.definitionFit: To crib is to copy someone else's work and pass it off as your own.

clue.text: Bird on Channel Islands returning to be seen in colder seas

definitions.text: to be seen in colder seas

indicators.note: the bird and the islands are read back the other way
in a down clue the bird sits on top of the islands

parts.note: a grebe is a diving water bird

explanation.surface: A seabird on Jersey or Guernsey heading back to cold northern waters.
explanation.walkthrough: CI stands for the Channel Islands, such as Jersey and Guernsey, off the coast of France.
explanation.definitionFit: Icebergs are huge floating blocks of ice found in polar and cold waters.

clue.text: She is a star in Italy

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the Italian word for star

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a famous actress in Italy; it is the name and the Italian word.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a female first name, and the Italian noun for a celestial star.

clue.text: Disorganised TT races ran, but start was wet

indicators.note: colours that ran have run into a new arrangement, so these letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word but

parts.note: the first letter of the word but
it rained when the weather was wet

explanation.surface: The Isle of Man TT motorbike races went ahead even though it started raining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ran' looks like a verb for the races; it is the signal to rearrange them.
explanation.definitionFit: A scatterbrained person is muddled and forgetful, unable to keep things in order.

clue.text: Notice blemish

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to see or catch sight of
second meaning: a mark or pimple on the skin

explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb meaning to catch sight of and a noun for a small mark.

clue.text: Work-shy take unemployment benefit into pub at opening time

indicators.note: the benefit is put into the pub

parts.note: an inn is a pub
the dole is British slang for unemployment benefit

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word time

parts.note: the first letter of the word time

explanation.surface: A lazy person takes the dole money straight to the pub at opening time.
explanation.walkthrough: The dole is British unemployment benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: An indolent person is lazy and avoids effort, so is reluctant to work.

clue.text: Surrender to despair

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to yield or quit
second meaning: to lose all hope

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as yielding to despair; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrasal verb means both to stop resisting and to abandon hope.

clue.text: Told story of knave in Arden ruined

indicators.note: the knave goes inside the rearranged place name
a ruined Arden has had its letters knocked about

parts.note: taken as written
a rat is a scoundrel or knave

explanation.surface: Someone recounted a tale of a rogue whose life was wrecked in the Forest of Arden.
explanation.walkthrough: Arden is Shakespeare's forest in As You Like It.
explanation.definitionFit: To narrate an event is to recount it, telling the story of it.

clue.text: Fear loud Conservatives

parts.note: F is forte, loud in music
the political right are the conservatives

explanation.surface: A worry about noisy Tory politicians.
explanation.definitionFit: A fright is a sudden feeling of alarm or terror.
